akhfash:2-2.t: He said ﴿جَمَعَ﴾ and ﴿جَمَعَ مَالاً وَعَدَّدَهُ﴾: from "العِدَّة" (number, counting).

akhfash:3-4.t: [And He said] ﴿يَحْسَبُ أَنَّ مَالَهُ أَخْلَدَهُ﴾ ﴿كَلاَّ لَيُنبَذَنَّ فِي ٱلْحُطَمَةِ﴾, that is: he and his wealth.

akhfash:8-8.t: And He said ﴿مُّؤْصَدَةٌ﴾: from "أَأْصَدَ" "يُؤصِدُ"; and some say "أُوْصِدَتْ", and that one is not pronounced with hamza, like "أَوْجَعَ", so "مُوجع". Similarly "أَأْكَفَ" and "أَوْكَفَ" — both are said.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿وَيْلٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject), in the nominative (marfūʿ). ﴿لِكُلِّ﴾ its khabar (predicate). ﴿هُمَزَةٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿لُمَزَةٍ﴾ a badal (substitute) from it; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿الَّذِي﴾ a relative noun, a badal (substitute) of the whole for the whole (badal kull min kull). ﴿جَمَعَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿مالًا﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَعَدَّدَهُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿يَحْسَبُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿أَنَّ مالَهُ﴾ anna and its noun. ﴿أَخْلَدَهُ﴾ a past verb and its object, and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of anna, and the interpreted maṣdar (maṣdar muʾawwal) formed from anna and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of يحسب; the clause «يحسب..» is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ a particle of deterrence and rebuke (radʿ wa-zajr). ﴿لَيُنْبَذَنَّ﴾ the lām occurs in the response to an omitted oath, and a passive imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis; the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), and the clause is the response to the oath, with no grammatical position. ﴿فِي الْحُطَمَةِ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) what precedes them.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿نارُ اللَّهِ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿الْمُوقَدَةُ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of نار; the clause is a badal (substitute) from الحطمة.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿الَّتِي﴾ a relative noun, an adjective (ṣifa) of نار. ﴿تَطَّلِعُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿عَلَى الْأَفْئِدَةِ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿إِنَّها﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate). ﴿مُؤْصَدَةٌ﴾ khabar; the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿فِي عَمَدٍ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are an adjective (ṣifa) of مؤصدة. ﴿مُمَدَّدَةٍ﴾ an adjective of عمد.

farraa:1-1.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ويْلٌ لِّكُلِّ هُمَزَةٍ لُّمَزَةٍ﴾.
It was revealed only concerning one man who used to يهمز and يلمز people: to backbite them and find fault with them. It is permissible in Arabic to mention something general while you intend a single one of it; you would say in ordinary speech, when a man says: I will never visit you, — you say: كل من لم يزرنى فلست بزائره (whoever does not visit me, I will not visit him), meaning it as a reply and intending him. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: Ibn Masʿūd] it is: "وَيْلٌ لِلْهُمَزَةِ اللُّمَزَةِ".

farraa:2-2.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلَّذِى جَمَعَ مَالاً﴾.
Al-Aʿmash and Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī made it heavy: «جمّع»; ʿĀṣim, Nāfiʿ and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī made it light. They all agreed on ﴿وَعَدَّدَهُ﴾ with shadda, meaning: he counted it. Al-Ḥasan read it "وعدَدَه", light; and some of them said, concerning the one who read it light: he gathered wealth and counted his number (عدده) — light — meaning his kinsfolk.

farraa:3-3.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَحْسَبُ أَنَّ مَالَهُ أَخْلَدَهُ﴾.
He means: يخلده (will make him immortal). You might say to a man: أتحسب أنّ مالك أنجاك من عذاب الله؟ ما أنجاك من عذابه إلاّ الطاعة (Do you think your wealth has saved you from Allah's punishment? Nothing has saved you from His punishment except obedience), and you mean: ما ينجيك (nothing will save you). Of the same kind is your saying of a man who commits a ruinous sin: دخل والله النار (By Allah, he has entered the Fire), and the meaning is: the Fire has become due to him.

farraa:4-4.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَيُنبَذَنَّ فِي ٱلْحُطَمَةِ﴾.
The generality read it: "لَيُنْبَذَنَّ", in the singular, and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī alone read it [148/b] "لَيُنْبَذَانِّ فى الحطمة" (the two shall surely be flung into al-Ḥuṭama), meaning: the man and his wealth. «الحطمة» is one of the names of the Fire, like His saying: جهنم, سقر and لظى. If you dropped the alif and lām from it, since it is a proper name, it would not take tanwīn (lam yajri, i.e. it would be a diptote).

farraa:7-7.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تَطَّلِعُ عَلَى ٱلأَفْئِدَةِ﴾.
He says: its pain reaches the hearts. «الاطلاع» and «البلوغ» (reaching) may have one meaning. The Arabs say: متى طلعتَ أرضنا (when did you reach our land?) and طلعتُ أرضى (I reached my land), i.e.: reached.

farraa:8-8.t:
His words, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿مُّؤْصَدَةٌ﴾.
It is the one closed over [them]; it is pronounced with hamza and without hamza.

farraa:9-9.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فِي عَمَدٍ مُّمَدَّدَةِ﴾.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us; he said: Muḥammad narrated to us;] he said: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us; he said: Ismāʿīl ibn Jaʿfar al-Madanī narrated to me; he said: Our companions used to read: (فى عَمَد) with fatḥa [Translator's note: the source says «بالنصب», i.e. with fatḥa on the ʿayn and mīm], and so did al-Ḥasan. And al-Kisāʾī narrated it to me from Sulaymān ibn Arqam, from al-Ḥasan: (فى عَمَد).
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us; he said: Muḥammad narrated to us;] he said: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us; he said: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ narrated to me from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamra al-Salūlī, from ʿAlī, may Allah have mercy on him, that he read it: "فى عُمُد مُمَدَّدَةٍ".
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us; he said: Muḥammad narrated to us;] he said: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us; he said: Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl narrated to me from ʿAṭāʾ, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd and Zayd ibn Thābit, that they both read: "فى عُمُد مُمَدَّدَة".
Al-Farrāʾ said: «العُمُد» and «العَمَد» are two plurals of «العمود» (pillar), like: الأديم, الأُدُم and الأَدَم (hide); الإهَاب, الأُهُب and الأَهَب (skin); and القضيم, القَضَم and القُضُم. And it is said: they are pillars of fire.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Humaza
Meccan
﷽
His saying: ﴿وَيْلٌ لِكُلِّ هُمَزَةٍ لُمَزَةٍ﴾ ("woe to every slanderer, backbiter"): ”وَيْلٌ“ is nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is ﴿لِكُلِّ هُمَزَةٍ﴾. If it were outside the Qur'an the accusative would be permissible, but it is not permissible in the Qur'an because it would contradict the Muṣḥaf. Whoever says ”وَيْلًا لِلْكافِرِينَ“ ("woe to the unbelievers", accusative), the meaning is: "Allah has assigned him woe"; and whoever says ”وَيْلٌ“, that is better in Arabic, because woe has been established for him. ”اَلْوَيْلُ“ is a word said to everyone who has fallen into ruin. ”اَلْهُمَزَةُ اللُّمَزَةُ“ is the one who backbites people and disparages them. The poet said:
إذا لَقِيتُكَ عَنْ كُرْهٍ تُكاشِرُنِي ∗∗∗ وإنْ تَغَيَّبْتُ كُنْتَ الهامِزَ اللُّمَزَةْ
(When I meet you, you grin at me grudgingly; and if I am absent, you are the slanderer, the backbiter.)
It was read: ”اَلَّذِي جَمَّعَ مالًا“ ("who amassed wealth", with doubling), and it was read: ﴿جَمَعَ مالا﴾ [al-Humaza: 2] with the light [mīm]. And it was read: ﴿وَعَدَّدَهُ﴾ [al-Humaza: 2] with the doubled [dāl], and it was read: ”وَعَدَدَهُ“ with the light [dāl]. Whoever reads ﴿وَعَدَّدَهُ﴾ [al-Humaza: 2], its meaning is: and counted it [as provision] for the ages; and whoever reads ﴿وَعَدَّدَهُ﴾ [al-Humaza: 2], its meaning is: he gathered wealth and numbers (ʿadad), that is, and people whom he prepared as helpers. [Translator's note: the second ﴿وَعَدَّدَهُ﴾ is evidently meant to be the light reading «وَعَدَدَهُ», as the explanation "wealth and numbers" shows.]

zajjaj:3-3.t: And His saying: ﴿يَحْسَبُ أنَّ مالَهُ أخْلَدَهُ﴾ ("he thinks that his wealth has made him immortal"): that is, he acts as one acts who, with his affluence, does not think that he will die.

zajjaj:4-4.t: And His saying: ﴿لَيُنْبَذَنَّ في الحُطَمَةِ﴾ ("he will surely be flung into the Crusher"): that is, he will be thrown into the Fire. ”اَلْحُطَمَةُ“ is one of the names of the Fire. It was also read: ”لَيُنْبَذانِّ في الحُطَمَةِ“ (dual), and it is related from al-Ḥasan, on the meaning: "he and his wealth will surely be flung into the Crusher". And it was read: ”لَتُنْبَذُنَّ في الحُطَمَةِ“, whose meaning is that he will be flung, he and what he gathered, into the Crusher. [Translator's note: so in the source; the vowelling of «لَتُنْبَذُنَّ» as printed (second person) does not match the explanation given, and may be corrupt.] The well-known reading is ﴿لَيُنْبَذَنَّ﴾.

zajjaj:6-7.t: His saying: ﴿نارُ اللَّهِ المُوقَدَةُ﴾ ﴿الَّتِي تَطَّلِعُ عَلى الأفْئِدَةِ﴾ ("the kindled Fire of Allah, which rises over the hearts"): this is a Fire prepared for these unbelievers and those like them. And the meaning of ﴿تَطَّلِعُ عَلى الأفْئِدَةِ﴾ is: its pain and its burning reach the hearts.

zajjaj:8-8.t: And His saying: ﴿إنَّها عَلَيْهِمْ مُؤْصَدَةٌ﴾ ("it will be closed down upon them"): it was read with hamza and without hamza; it was read ”مُوصَدَةٌ“. The Arabs say ”أوْصَدْتُهُ“, and according to this it is ”مُوصَدَةٌ“; and they say ”آصَدْتُهُ“, and according to this it is ”مُؤْصَدَةٌ“ with hamza. The meaning of ”مُوصَدَةٌ“ is "closed over", that is, the punishment is closed over them.

zajjaj:9-9.t: And His saying: ﴿فِي عَمَدٍ مُمَدَّدَةٍ﴾ ("in extended columns"): it was also read ”فِي عُمُدٍ“. It is the plural of ”عِمادٌ“: ”عُمَدٌ“ and ”عُمُدٌ“, as they said ”إهابٌ“ ("hide"), ”أُهَبٌ“ and ”أُهُبٌ“. Its meaning is that it is in columns of fire. [Translator's note: the source vowels the first plural «عُمَدٌ»; the Qur'anic reading discussed is «عَمَدٍ».]
